title: Fieldnote project file, schemaVersion 1 (frozen 2026-11-01, approved by Claude and Codex)
$comment: Rules JSON Schema cannot express, enforced by the app validator before any state is replaced: (1) the serialized UTF-8 project file is at most 26214400 bytes (25 MiB), checked on the raw file before parsing; (2) each image's DECODED bytes (base64 payload) are at most 2097152 (2 MiB) and must equal image.bytes; (3) width*height <= 16000000; (4) image.sha256 matches the decoded bytes; (5) the decoded bytes start with the PNG or JPEG signature matching mime, and the real dimensions match width/height; (6) every evidence id and logo id resolves to exactly one image, each image is referenced at most once, ids are unique; (7) a file with schemaVersion greater than 1 is refused as 'newer'; (8) the total number of evidence references across all findings is at most 30, with or without a logo; (9) project.nextFindingNumber is greater than the highest existing F-NNN suffix and project.nextImageNumber is greater than the highest existing IMG-NNNN suffix, and suffixes 000/0000 are never issued or accepted; (10) every string is valid XML 1.0 text: C0 control characters other than tab, LF and CR, U+FFFE/U+FFFF and unpaired surrogates cause the import to be refused (valid Unicode, including astral characters, is preserved unchanged); typed or pasted input is sanitized at entry by removing those characters. Text fields are plain text: blank line = new paragraph, a line starting with '- ' = bullet. Text is never interpreted as HTML.

nextFindingNumber.$comment: Counter for new finding ids. Ids are never reused or renumbered, even after deletion.

findings.$comment: Array order is report order. Display numbering in the DOCX follows the stable id, not the position.

severity.$comment: null = unscored; the pre-export checklist warns.

reproduction.$comment: Request/reproduction text, rendered in the code style.

images.$comment: At most 30 evidence images plus one optional logo. Images not referenced anywhere are refused on import and dropped on save.

tallMode.$comment: How the exporter handles an image taller than one page at full content width. 'fit' scales to the page; 'split' cuts into page-height parts captioned 'part n of m'. Never clipped silently.
